status_reason: A provisional assessment is justified because published laboratory precedent demonstrates the feasibility of combining MIR ATR and fluorescence using a single probe head for classifying chicken muscle, fat, and liver. However, a preliminary feasibility study only establishes proof of concept for the measurement interface and cannot demonstrate diagnostic utility or in vivo performance.

premise_checks.premise: Sequential measurements on heterogeneous tissue with separate probes may fail to sample the same location.
premise_checks.explanation: Published evaluations confirm that alternating separate probes on heterogeneous biological tissue cannot ensure identical measurement spots, necessitating co-located interfaces.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: An ATR immersion probe geometry featuring a truncated cone (frustum) crystal, such as ZrO2, allowing three internal reflections for MIR ATR at the facets and orthogonal fluorescence excitation and collection via integrated silica fibers through the flat crystal tip.
measurement_concept.location: Laboratory contact measurement directly placed onto excised tissue samples in petri dishes or sample holders.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: Chalcogenide infrared (CIR) fibers for the MIR ATR optical path and UV-Vis transmitting silica fibers for the fluorescence channel.

citations.quote: ZrO2 crystal was chosen due to its high (close to the diamond) refractive index, high transparency in the working spectral regions of both chalcogenide infrared (CIR) and UV silica fibers, as well as small intrinsic fluorescence.

A round platform at the top of the truncated cone simultaneously serves to record fluorescence spectra. Silica fiber end faces are located exactly below it, providing the orthogonal sample illumination and reception of the fluorescence signal emitted back by the sample.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If single-method MIR ATR fails to separate liver from muscle during initial testing, or if simultaneous co-located acquisition is confirmed feasible, the extended dual-method option O3 becomes preferred.
proposal.next_step: Run baseline single-method trials on chicken breast, fat, and liver specimens to establish benchmark separation before evaluating fused dual-method probe acquisitions.

brief_answer: Test single-method MIR ATR first on representative chicken muscle, fat, and liver samples, as it provides fundamental lipid and protein discrimination. Compare this against fluorescence spectroscopy, which selectively identifies liver porphyrin emission. Combining both methods into a co-located probe head is the recommended extended path if neither single method separates all three classes, as demonstrated in laboratory precedent. The interface architecture, excitation wavelength, and target accuracy criteria remain open.
